name: Terrace
description: Terrace is a two-deck solitaire for one player. Shuffle two decks; 11 cards face-up reserve, 8 foundation piles, 9 tableau piles. Deal 3 to three tableaus, choose one for first foundation (only that rank to foundations). Build foundations up in alternating colours (A between K and 2); tableaus down in alternating colours. Reserve: only top card to foundations. Empty tableau filled from stock or discard. Goal: move all 104 cards to foundations.

setup.players: One player. Terrace is a solitaire (two-deck patience) for a single player.
setup.deck: Two standard 52-card decks shuffled together (104 cards).
setup.dealing: Shuffle both decks. Lay 11 cards face-up in a row as the reserve. Below, eight empty foundation piles and nine empty tableau piles. Deal three cards from stock face-up, one to each of three tableaus. Choose one of these three to move to the first foundation; only cards of that rank may start other empty foundations. Deal seven more cards from stock, one onto each remaining empty tableau. Remaining cards form the stock (face-up, squared). Discard pile starts empty.
setup.equipment: Two decks, table space for reserve, eight foundations, nine tableaus, stock and discard.

rules.objective: Move all 104 cards to the eight foundation piles; the game is won when every card is on a foundation.
rules.gameplay: 1. Layout: 11-card reserve (face-up), eight foundations, nine tableaus, stock, discard. 2. Building: Foundations build up in alternating colors (red and black), circular order with Ace between King and 2, 13 cards per foundation. Tableaus build down in alternating colors. 3. Empty tableau rule: When any tableau is empty, it must be filled immediately with a card from the stock or the discard. 4. When no tableaus are empty (or stock and discard are both empty): top cards of tableaus may move to other tableaus or foundations; top card of reserve to foundations only; top card of stock or discard to tableaus or foundations. 5. Dealing: Play one card from the stock to the discard pile at any time, except when there is an empty tableau.
keyRules: Foundations: build up, alternating colors, circular (A between K and 2).
Tableaus: build down in alternating colors.
Empty tableau must be filled immediately from stock or discard.
Only the top card of the reserve may be played, and only to foundations.
One card from stock to discard allowed at any time except when a tableau is empty.

strategy.basic: When choosing the first foundation card, look at the reserve and choose a rank that lets you play the first reserve cards early and the last ones late.
strategy.intermediate: Moving cards from the reserve should be highest priority; look ahead for opportunities to move the top reserve cards and avoid plays that block them.
strategy.advanced: Keep the discard pile small. Fill empty tableaus from the discard unless filling from the stock lets you immediately play a card from the discard as well. Keep as many one-card tableaus as reasonable so they can be moved to create an empty pile.
tips: Choose the first foundation rank with the reserve in mind.
Prefer filling empty tableaus from discard unless stock fill enables an immediate discard play.
Keep one-card tableaus when possible to create empty piles.
